title: Eviction sandbox and consistency checker for prefix-aware LRU/TTL policies
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and prefix-aware prefetching are increasingly used, eviction decisions (LRU vs TTL vs prefix-grouping) are producing occasional user-facing regressions: stale prefix evictions, broken KV cache hits during multi-request batches, and OOM pressure spikes on specific GPU shapes. We need a way to safely iterate on eviction heuristics without risking production correctness and to provide deterministic guarantees for prefix-scoped state transitions.

Goal: Implement an 'eviction sandbox' mode and an offline/online consistency checker that together allow: (1) simulation of eviction actions against live traffic (shadow-execute without committing) to detect regressions; (2) verification of core invariants (no interleaving that can leave two concurrent requests with inconsistent prefix KV views, bounded staleness guarantees for TTL+LRU hybrid, and GPU memory accounting invariants); (3) a signal surface (metrics and traces) for safe rollout of new eviction policies.

Non-goals: This ticket is not a full rewrite of the eviction policy or a replacement for our lease/coordinator architecture. It focuses on simulation, invariants, and observability so changes can be validated prior to serving commits.
implementation_steps: Add a sandbox mode flag (env + per-route config) where eviction decisions are computed and logged but not applied to KV allocator; must support both per-shard and global modes.
Build a consistency checker service that consumes eviction traces and live access traces; checker should validate invariants and produce human-readable counter-examples when invariants fail.
Instrument batch executor to emit per-request prefix access sequences with timestamps and cache hit/miss info (compact binary protobuf + human JSON for debug).
Integrate GPU memory accounting with eviction simulator to compute projected vs actual memory deltas for each decision and detect under/over-commit patterns.

Create metrics: sandbox.eviction.simulated_total, sandbox.eviction.conflict_detected, sandbox.invariant.counterexample_rate, sandbox.projected_memory_delta_p50/p95, and alert rules for conflict_detected > 0 over 5m.

Add acceptance tests: microbench that reproduces previously observed regression patterns (long-tail prefix bursts, TTL expirations during large batches, concurrent prefix writes) and assert checker finds no invariant violations.
Expose a debug endpoint (admin) to run a focused sandbox replay for a specific shard/prefix and return a trace-level report.

Create rollout plan: enable sandbox for Canary pool, analyze results for 48h, then enable 'soft-apply' where simulated evictions are applied to a shadow copy with TTL-only fallback, then full apply if no regressions.
Document the sandbox mode and checker in the runtime runbook and add how-tos for platform engineers to triage counterexamples.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox mode computes eviction decisions and logs them without mutating allocator state when enabled.
Consistency checker runs in prod-readonly mode and emits human-readable counterexamples for any invariant violations within 5 minutes of detection.
Metric surface for sandbox and checker is available in the Console and dashboards (per-shard scoped) and integrated into alerting.
Automated tests reproduce two prior regression cases and the checker flags counterexamples for both in CI when sandbox is enabled.
Canary rollout plan validated: canary pool runs for 48h with sandbox enabled and yields no critical counterexamples before soft-apply.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sandbox mode to ensure no allocator writes occur (mock allocator assertions).
Integration test that replays recorded high-concurrency traces into sandbox and verifies computed decisions match a golden oracle for baseline policy.
Fuzzy/chaos tests that inject clock skews and simulated slow evictions to check checker resilience and avoid false positives.
Performance benchmark: ensure sandbox instrumentation increases p50 latency by <1% and p99 by <3% in canary cluster; measure logging overhead and sampling configuration.
Manual acceptance: run debug endpoint for a suspicious shard, confirm counterexample explains a previous live regression.
risks: Sandbox logging and trace export could add observable overhead or I/O pressure if not sampled carefully.
False positives from the checker (e.g., due to clock skew or multi-region replication delay) could block valid policy changes; we must provide debug tooling to triage quickly.
Complexity of mapping simulated eviction timeline to live memory accounting for GPU shapes may yield mismatches; we will validate with microbenchmarks per-shape.
Rolling out soft-apply incorrectly could cause double-free or race conditions unless allocator snapshotting is robust.
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after post-mortem on P0 incident where a TTL sweep raced with a large batch and caused two user requests to observe inconsistent prefix state. Added goals and non-goals.

2025-02-18 Marco Chen: Spike implemented a prototype sandbox that shadow-runs eviction decisions and writes a compact trace. Early results show sandbox adds ~0.6% p50 overhead when sampling at 5% per-shard.
2025-02-25 SRE (Lena Ortiz): Observability integration looks good, requested a guardrail to disable sandbox trace export automatically if IO backlog > 2000 msgs/min.
2025-03-01 Marco Chen: Pushed initial PR for the sandbox flag and trace schema (see related PR); starting integration tests for the checker. Adding a small protobuf as the canonical trace payload.

2025-03-04 Aisha Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria to require human-readable counterexamples in checker output and added canary rollout steps. Scheduling cross-team review with Infra and SRE next week.
